claims.text: As-cast or homogenized HfNbTaTiZr has a uniform matrix with minimal nanoprecipitate formation.
Controlled aging or annealing can induce coherent nanoprecipitates in HfNbTaTiZr.
Comparing precipitate-bearing samples with untreated samples under otherwise identical thermal cycles is intended to isolate the effect of engineered nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates and their matrix have differing thermal-expansion coefficients.
Thermal-expansion mismatch at precipitate–matrix interfaces generates internal residual stresses during thermal cycling.
Precipitate-associated residual stresses control the stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
The residual stresses alter dislocation mobility by impeding or facilitating dislocation motion.
The residual stresses influence phase stability.
A common residual-stress mechanism can unify the alloy's reported creep, microhardness, and elastic-modulus behavior.
Aged samples containing nanoprecipitates will have higher residual stresses than as-cast samples.
Nanoprecipitate-bearing aged samples will have greater strength than the as-cast baseline.
The enhanced strength of aged samples results from thermal-expansion-mismatch residual stresses.
Aged samples with nanoprecipitates will exhibit decreased creep at approximately 1250 °C relative to as-cast samples.
Aged samples with nanoprecipitates will exhibit altered elastic moduli over 293–1100 K relative to as-cast samples.
Residual-stress differences will correlate with differences in dislocation dynamics observed through microhardness and tensile testing.
Thermoelastic effects should be most prominent below approximately 1100 K.
Residual-stress effects on creep should be prominent near 1250 °C and may be negligible outside the specified temperature regions.
Residual-stress profiling, creep testing, elastic-modulus measurements, and microscopy can jointly test the proposed causal chain.
Failure to observe residual-stress differences or statistically distinguishable creep and elastic-modulus responses would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
